action: Upgrade React and Next.js to fixed versions; until then strip or reject the x-middleware-subrequest header at the proxy or WAF, check logs for it and for /_next/image requests aimed at the metadata address, rotate every secret the server could reach, and enforce IMDSv2.
attack: T1552.005 Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API
date_note: Date of OpenSourceMalware's published research; the repositories were created in waves from October 22.
exec: Stolen server secrets from Next.js sites are being committed to public GitHub repositories, so anyone can read them; unpatched sites are exposed.
geo_basis: GitHub, the platform hosting the campaign (no victim location stated)
plain: OpenSourceMalware reports a campaign that scans websites built with Next.js for known flaws and saves any stolen secrets in public GitHub repositories. Both flaws have had patches for months.

key_findings: OpenSourceMalware named the campaign React2STEAL and identified 45 repositories across 44 GitHub accounts running a scan.yml GitHub Actions workflow.

The pipeline tries React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182), the CVE-2025-29927 middleware bypass and an SSRF through /_next/image to cloud instance metadata, then collects environment variables, credentials and config files.
At least 1,281 unique victim hostnames across about 1,100 domains were found; results were still being committed about every 11 minutes on November 17.
OpenSourceMalware lists the threat actor as unknown and says it does not know whether the same operator ran the earlier wfx-loot campaign.
recommendations: Upgrade React and Next.js to fixed versions.
Strip or reject x-middleware-subrequest at the proxy or WAF until upgraded.
Rotate every secret the server could reach and enforce IMDSv2.

summary: OpenSourceMalware published research on November 18 on a campaign it named React2STEAL: 45 GitHub repositories across 44 accounts run scanners for React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) and CVE-2025-29927 and commit results to public repositories. It found at least 1,281 victim hostnames across about 1,100 domains. It lists the actor as unknown. GitGuardian's write-up says patches for both flaws have been available for months.
title: React2STEAL: GitHub Actions scanners exploit React2Shell and publish stolen secrets

validation.note: Read OpenSourceMalware's research and GitGuardian's write-up (via Security Boulevard); the primary source states the core facts.
